subtopics.title: Naming the Variables and Finding the Rule

questions.question: In the plumber's charge, the independent and dependent variables are:
options: Independent = number of hours worked; dependent = the cost of the job
Independent = the cost of the job; dependent = number of hours worked
Independent = the call-out fee; dependent = the hourly rate

questions.question: The plumber charges R400 call-out plus R260 per hour. The formula is:
Using that formula, a four-hour job costs:
A constant difference between consecutive values in a table tells you the relationship is:
options: Linear — the same amount is added for each extra unit, so the graph is a straight line

subtopics.title: When the Difference Is Not Constant

questions.question: R2 400 bakkie hire split equally: 1 person pays R2 400, 2 pay R1 200, 3 pay R800, 4 pay R600. This is inverse proportion because:
options: The PRODUCT of people and cost per person is always R2 400
The graph is a straight line

questions.question: With eight people sharing the R2 400 bakkie, each pays:
R5 000 grows to R5 300, then R5 618, then R5 955,08. The rule is:
options: Multiply by 1,06 each year — a constant ratio between consecutive terms

questions.question: The routine for testing a table, in order, is:
options: Draw the graph, then guess the shape
Divide the last value by the first
Differences constant? Then products constant? Then ratios constant?

questions.question: The three representations of one relationship are:
options: The formula (or equation), the table of values, and the graph
The mean, the median and the mode
The fixed charge, the rate and the total
The heading, the axes and the scale

questions.question: Points for the number of people in the bakkie are plotted but NOT joined because:
options: The graph would be too long
The data is DISCRETE — there is no such thing as 3,5 people

questions.question: An inverse-proportion relationship graphs as:
options: A straight line through the origin
A rising curve that gets steeper
A falling curve that flattens, approaching the axes without touching them

questions.question: To read a value off a graph correctly you should:
options: Go up from the horizontal axis to the line, straight across to the vertical axis, and state the units

subtopics.title: Working Backwards on a Combination Tariff

questions.question: Water costs R160,00 basic charge plus R24,50 per kℓ. A household using 12 kℓ pays:
The bill is R699,00. The correct first step to find the kilolitres used is:
options: Subtract the R160,00 basic charge first, leaving R539,00 that paid for water

questions.question: That R699,00 bill corresponds to a usage of:
Which set of habits protects marks in this topic?
options: Round every line of working to the nearest rand
Divide the total by the rate every time
Write the formula, show the substitution, keep the units, round only at the end, and answer in a sentence

questions.question: The two questions to ask of any price list are:
options: What do I pay before anything happens, and what does each extra unit add?
Who is charging, and where do they live?
What is the average, and what is the range?
Is it discrete, and is it continuous?

questions.question: In the plumber's bill, the R400 and the R260 behave differently because:
options: The R400 sits still while the R260 multiplies by the number of hours
The R260 is charged only once
They are added together at the start

questions.question: Hours go along the bottom of the graph and rands up the side because:
options: You choose the hours, and the money follows from that choice

subtopics.title: Splitting the Bakkie, Growing the Stokvel

questions.question: Going from one passenger to two saves R1 200 each, but going from five to six saves only R80 each. This is because:
options: The bakkie's price never moves — it is only shared further, so the saving per extra person shrinks
The driver charges more for a full load
The rate per person is constant

questions.question: The stokvel's jumps grow — R300, then R318, then R337,08 — because:
options: The interest rate rises each year
In the second year interest is earned on R5 300, not just on the original R5 000
Extra money is deposited each year

questions.question: The multiplying test for the bakkie table means:
options: Multiply the first and last values
Multiply the number of people by the price each pays — you always land back on R2 400
Multiply the difference by the number of rows

questions.question: A table whose values will not add nicely should be tested by:
options: Multiplying across each pair, then dividing each value by the one before it

questions.question: Dividing the whole R699 bill by R24,50 is wrong because:
options: It pretends the R160 basic charge bought water, when it paid for the pipes, meter and connection
Division is never used in tariffs
The answer would be too small

questions.question: The check that the answer of 22 kℓ is right is:
options: Going forwards again: R160 plus twenty-two lots of R24,50 is R699 exactly
Comparing it with last month's bill

questions.question: One kilolitre of water is:
The proper way to finish the answer is:
options: Write a sentence: the household used 22 kilolitres of water that month
